title: Color grading engine: curves and tonal-range tools
base: codex/color-grading-cg3 ff4ded57, with PR #77's tip 50e5d033 (D65 white balance) merged in

environment.referenceGenerators: scipy 1.18.1 (PchipInterpolator) via the CG0 vector generator (development only)

delivered.splines: PCHIP (Fritsch-Carlson monotone cubic Hermite, Fritsch-Butland derivatives) matching scipy within 1e-12; periodic hue curves; baked to 1024-entry float32 tables with linear extrapolation

effects.grade.curves: red, green, blue then master curves; lumaMix 0-1 (master on luma only, chroma kept)
effects.grade.hue-curves: hueVsHue, hueVsSat, hueVsLum, lumVsSat, satVsSat, satVsLum in BT.709 Y'CbCr, y = 0.5 neutral
effects.grade.tonal: shadow/mid/highlight RGB offsets and exposure (stops) with shadowEnd, highlightStart and falloff, then C1 high and low soft clip

delivered.gpu: curve tables uploaded as one RGBA8 texture whose texels carry each float32's bits (read back exactly with uintBitsToFloat); sampled as the reference does
delivered.notInPlanWording: the plan names 'saturation vs luminance' and the five hue/saturation curves; all six are in grade.hue-curves. Zone-based exposure is per range (three zones), not the ten zones of the CG3 exposure scope.

checks.check: Identity curves are exact identities; spline evaluation matches reference vectors; no overshoot outside the control hull for monotone inputs
checks.evidence: identity (and flat hue) curves give null controls, so the operator is dropped and pixels are unchanged on both backends (browser 'neutral' case); 10 spline cases within 1e-12 of scipy, periodic included; 500 seeded monotone curves sampled at 2001 points stay within each segment's control range and never decrease

checks.check: Each hue/saturation curve changes only its target dimension on the sweep fixtures, within tolerance (measured with CG3)
checks.evidence: float64: on the CG0 hue sweep, saturation sweep and skin tones, off-target vectorscope angle, chroma radius and luma move by < 1e-9 (radius, luma) or 1e-6 degrees (angle). Rendered (both backends), measured with the CG3 functions (vectorscopeAngle, chroma709, encodedLuma) on pixels whose float result stays in 0-1: off-target luma <= 0.0019 (half an 8-bit step), off-target radius <= 0.0020, off-target angle <= 1.7 degrees (skin tones, low chroma), while the target dimension moves by 90 degrees, 0.04-0.17 radius or 0.10-0.13 luma
checks.note: On fully saturated hue-sweep colors a hue rotation can leave the gamut; the 8-bit output clips those values and then moves every dimension. They are excluded from the rendered measurement and counted (clipped in benchmarks/results/color-grading-cg4/curves.json); the float64 measurement covers every pixel.

checks.check: Hue curves are continuous across the 0 deg/360 deg wrap
checks.evidence: float64: |f(1 - 1e-9) - f(0)| < 1e-8; a colour 0.02 degrees either side of +Cb keeps its chroma within 1e-5; rendered: the step across the hue sweep's wrap is no larger than its neighbours' step on both backends

checks.check: Animated curve points keep the existing ordering and point-count rules
checks.evidence: the CG4 curves use the existing curve parameter: animated y validates and evaluates; a keyed curve whose point count changes is rejected; endpoints away from 0/1 and 17 points are rejected; an animated x that crosses its neighbour fails at the crossing frame ('strictly increasing'); periodic hue curves with different end y and tonal ranges out of order fail with comp-effect-params

parity.layerKinds: 81 cases, 972 frames, backend difference <= 1 (animated curve points included)

failedRunsAndReruns: Unit tests were written first and all 26 failed before the module existed.

Unit run 2: the no-overshoot test failed on its own segment lookup (x = 1 fell back to the first segment) and the baked-table bound (1e-6) failed at 1.01e-6; the lookup was fixed and the bound set to 1e-5 from the measurement.
Unit run 3: the no-overshoot test timed out (3 million expect calls); it now counts violations and asserts once, and sorts numerically (the default sort compared strings).
Browser test before the CG4 kernels (HEAD renderer): failed with 'OPERATORS[id] is not a function' (failing first).

Browser run 1: hueVsHue changed the chroma radius by 0.34 on the rendered hue sweep: rotated saturated colors leave the gamut and the 8-bit output clips them. The rendered separation check now measures in-gamut pixels and counts the clipped ones.

Curve rules test: a static endpoint error is reported by the shared curve schema as its union's 'Invalid input', not the endpoint message; the test asserts the rejection (existing behaviour, as for color.curves).
CE6 coverage unit test failed until the new catalogue-curve-grade cell existed.

verification.checkFast: passed first time: 476 test files, 4,910 tests

browser.color-grading-cg2: passed (88 rows) with the shared GLSL extended
browser.composition-effects: curve-grade baseline written then checked; frozen CE6 and CG2 float-grade baselines unchanged

verification.notRunHere: composition-baselines (no grade effects in them; run at the end of CG5)

notRun: pnpm check, full pnpm test, runtime tier, release checks
